options: No, strings are not treated as sequences by match

questions.explanation: str, bytes and bytearray are deliberately excluded from sequence patterns.

questions.question: Does a match statement fall through to the next case after one matches?
options: No, only the first matching case runs
questions.explanation: There is no fall-through and no break in match.

questions.question: Which subjects does `case {"type": "expense", "amount": a}:` match? (select all)

questions.question: What type is `rest` after `case [first, *rest]:` matches (1, 2, 3)?

questions.explanation: Star captures in sequence patterns always produce a list.

questions.question: What is the problem with `case int:`?
options: It is a capture named int that matches everything
It matches only the int class itself
questions.explanation: Use case int(): to check the type; a bare name captures.

questions.question: What does `|` mean inside a case pattern?
options: Pipe the value into the next case
questions.explanation: case 401 | 403 | 404: matches any of the three values.

questions.question: What is a guard in a case clause?
options: An if condition after the pattern that must also be true
questions.explanation: case (x, y) if x == y: matches only when the pattern fits AND the condition holds.

questions.question: Why do dataclasses support positional class patterns like `case Point(0, y):`?

questions.question: If no case matches and there is no wildcard, what happens?
options: Nothing; execution continues after the match
questions.explanation: An unmatched match statement simply does nothing.
